title: Roll It Between Your Palms
text: “While this is information I’ve confirmed, my daughter Malty is currently missing, and we haven’t even heard anything suggesting she’s headed toward Faubrey.”
“It scares me to think she might secretly slip across the border to meet him.”
“That’s why I have no intention of letting my guard down. I trust what Mr. Iwatani and Mr. Kitamura have told me.”

Well, I suppose it won’t be a problem. After all, Crimson Swine is no longer among the living. The real issue is the one who plans to use Takt. Will we be able to handle him properly? To be honest, I think he’ll be even harder to deal with than Ren or Itsuki. As I tilted my head in thought, my Father gave a wry, uncertain smile.
“They’ve said they’re sending the Seven Star Hero over here… I’m worried, but even the Whip Hero wouldn’t suddenly do something foolish, would he? Given the gravity of the situation.”
“Hmm…”

I don’t quite get it. That guy isn’t the type you can reason with. Isn’t the life of the Seven Star Hero he’s bringing along in greater danger? To begin with, when we went to Siltvelt, he already had three Seven Star Weapons. Doesn’t that mean those two are already dead?
Just then, my eyes fell on the representative from Siltvelt. Should I bring this up now? I suppose I should confirm it.
“Are you saying the… Claw Hero from Siltvelt is coming too?”
“Yes. We’ve received word that our country’s hero will also be present.”

This is totally suspicious. It might be in our best interest to just kill them the moment we run into them. My Father has already explained the situation to the Siltvelt representative as well. He’s looking at me as if I’m up to no good, but I’m not lying.
“Since this concerns the Spear Hero, whom the Shield Hero trusts… let’s believe it. Then, I’ll pass on the message—”
“Wait. Just to be safe, I’d like you to keep this under wraps until the Seven Star Heroes arrive.”
“I understand your reasoning, but I’d like to verify it.”

The elderly Gemu is asking Father. That’s only natural. There’s no way we can do something as foolish as leaking this information to Takt and his companions. Whether we can use it or not, we can’t pass this information on.
“…You guys have a history of waging war against the Wise King of Wisdom, right? Isn’t it a bit odd to ask the other side, ‘You seem suspicious’?”

“That’s true. But our country’s Seven Star Heroes are, so to speak, representatives of the nation… Even if the words come from the Shield Hero, who is practically a god, it’s a bit difficult to accept them without verification.”
“I understand. We’ll probably meet face-to-face at some point, so I think it’ll be fine if you’re present then. Until then, keep this under wraps.”
“It’s likely that a monster with exceptional shape-shifting abilities has disguised itself as the Claw Hero.”
I told them about the fox that had disguised itself as the Spear Hero using the Beast Spear. I also mentioned that the fox was one of Takt’s companions.
“If this spear reacts, it’s definitely the real deal.”
If the Seven Star Heroes are coming here, I’ll handle them myself. Of course, I’ll let them run free for now, but if they make a single wrong move, I’ll eliminate them.
“Then let us make preparations so we can discreetly inform the King of Faubrey.”
“What are you going to do?”

“In the event of a problem, we’ll arrange for representatives from Melromarc and Siltvelt to join forces and ensure Faubrey takes action to quell the situation before Shieldfreeden and other factions intervene.”
“Is that really going to work?”
“Yes. Please think of it purely as a precaution.”

It seems the Queen has a plan of her own as well. For now, we’ve suspended our attempts to challenge the Spirit Tortoise and the Phoenix until the Seven Star Heroes arrive. My Father says he intends to use that fellow, so I’d prefer to settle this peacefully if possible.
“Then… to ensure we can launch our operation at any time, Motoyasu and I will set up portals as close as possible to the Phoenix and the Spirit Tortoise.”
“Understood.”
Then, with Filolial-sama’s cooperation, we set out to secure a location from which to carry out our operation.
The next day. An airship arrived in the skies above Melromarc. There are a few other airplanes here as well.

There are two airships… I see. Keel spotted them, pointed at them with a hint of excitement, and called out to my Father. We’re watching from the castle terrace as the airships land on the grassy plain.
“Bro, bro! This is awesome! So there really are things like that besides dragons and Airwake ore!”
“Yeah, seeing airships in another world… it’s kind of moving, isn’t it? Though you could also call it a bit jarring.”
“But since we’re summoning people from another world, isn’t it actually not that strange?” my Father murmured.
“Melty, have you ever seen an airship before?”
“Oh, yes. I’ve heard they’re vehicles developed in Faubrey. I saw one under construction before. I also saw one on a test flight from a distance.”
“Huh…”
“Faubrey, huh. I’ve been there before, but that kind of fancy stuff isn’t really my thing.”
The panda beastman is squinting as she stares at the airship.
“Lars-chan is a mercenary, after all. What’s Faubrey like?”
“That country’s a melting pot of races, so you’ll never get bored. After all, it is the center of the world, one way or another.”
“It sounds like a fun country… I can see why.”

Since I’ve been telling him about events from the future, my Father knows the dark side of Faubrey. Sure, on the surface, it’s a developed country. It doesn’t have that backwater feel that Melromarc has. Well, even so, compared to Japan, it’s on a whole different level—one that makes you snort in derision.
“Trade is brisk there, and, all things considered, new technologies often originate in Faubrey. But I definitely prefer Zeltoble.”
“Isn’t that the country of mercenaries?”

“That’s right. To be precise, it’s a country founded by mercenaries, and it’s also a nation of merchants. It’s a melting pot of races in a different sense than Faubrey. I just feel more at home over there.”

I guess it just depends on the person. Gambling is big in Zeltoble, after all. It’s a country that draws people in a different direction than a nation like Faubrey, which develops through cutting-edge technology.

If you ask me which country is better for making money, it’s definitely Zeltoble. There are underground guilds, and there’s the Colosseum. On top of that, there are even races where people compete by racing their Filolial-sama. Zeltoble also has a better weapons market.

Faubrey is a country where novel types of weapons are sold. If you think back to when it was a game, it’s the kind of place where newly implemented weapons end up on store shelves. Firearms are a prime example.
“Boo!”
“Huh? Elena, do you prefer Faubrey? Why?”
“Boo.”
“Ah… yeah, the spa. Yeah, that’s so Elena.”

Come to think of it, the Lazy Pig did go to the spa with the Crimson Swine, didn’t she? I suppose Faubrey’s advanced in that sort of technology as well. You could think of Faubrey as the artistic side and Zeltoble as the instinctive side.
“Hmm?”
Sakura-chan is staring at the airship.
“I get a bad feeling about this…”
“It feels kind of intimidating—”

After all, Takt has dragons in his entourage. And since they’re supposedly the Dragon Emperor—who’s practically the strongest of them all—even our Rival must be sensing his presence from afar. Yuki-chan and the others are also vaguely sensing that ominous vibe.
“So? What are we supposed to do now?”
“We’ve been told to meet up with the Seven Star Hero immediately for a strategy meeting. After that, we’re supposed to start moving right away.”
“Out of the blue? Aren’t they going to grant us an audience first?”
We were summoned in a similar way last time, after all. We should probably be on high alert.
“Since Faubrey has the upper hand in terms of national power, it really depends on their mood.”

“We’re supposed to show respect to the Four Saints, but the current arrangement came about because someone said, ‘If we have time for an audience, we should be taking action to minimize the damage as much as possible.’”
“Well… I suppose that makes sense. Let’s go, then. Either way, the Seven Star Heroes don’t have the means to defeat us, so we should be able to handle whatever comes our way.”

We could easily manipulate them like playthings at this point. It’s a good opportunity to gauge the extent of their intelligence capabilities. Despite our uneasy premonitions, we headed toward the airship together with the representatives from Melromarc and Siltvelt.
